We can also consider the generating function for the power sums:
$$
\sum_{m=1}^\infty S_m x^m = \sum_{m=1}^\infty m x^m = \frac{x}{(1 - x)^2}, \quad \text{for } |x| < 1.
$$
On the other hand, interchanging the order of summation gives:
$$
\sum_{m=1}^\infty \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n^m x^m = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{m=1}^\infty (a_n x)^m = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{a_n x}{1 - a_n x}.
$$
So we must have:
$$
\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{a_n x}{1 - a_n x} = \frac{x}{(1 - x)^2}.
$$
This is a functional equation that must hold for all $ |x| < r $, for some $ r > 0 $.
